title: Part 4 — Talk 6: project status update
instructionsVi: Cập nhật tiến độ. Có một chuỗi nhân quả nhiều bước — nghe hụt một mắt xích là mất câu trả lời.
promptEn: Listen to the update and answer questions 86 through 88.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Quick status on the Fairport fit-out before we go into detail.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: We finished the survey two weeks early, which gave us a buffer. We then used most of that buffer, because the concrete pour was delayed twice by frost.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Net effect: the foundations finished about ten days late rather than two weeks early. The frame was due to start on the first of February and will now begin on the eleventh.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: The steel supplier has confirmed they can hold our delivery slot, so we are not losing further time there.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: What I need from this room is the interior specification signed off before the frame is complete, not after — the electrical routing depends on it. If that slips past the end of March, we lose the summer completion date entirely, and that is not recoverable.

questions.prompt: 86. What caused the delay to the foundations?

options.text: Frost delayed the concrete pour twice.
The steel supplier missed a delivery.
The specification was not signed off.

questions.explanationVi: 'the concrete pour was delayed twice by frost'. Khảo sát xong SỚM hai tuần, không phải chậm.

questions.prompt: 87. On which date will the frame now start?
questions.explanationVi: 'due to start on the first of February and will now begin on the eleventh'.

questions.prompt: 88. Why must the specification be signed off before the frame is complete?

options.text: The electrical routing depends on it.
The survey has to be repeated otherwise.

questions.explanationVi: 'signed off before the frame is complete, not after — the electrical routing depends on it'.

title: Part 4 — Talk 7: museum orientation
instructionsVi: Bài mở đầu tham quan. Điều được phép và điều bị cấm nằm sát nhau trong cùng một câu.
promptEn: Listen to the orientation talk and answer questions 89 through 91.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Welcome to the Riverside Industrial Museum. I'll keep this short so you have time in the galleries.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Three floors. Ground floor is the mills, first floor is the people who worked in them, second floor is temporary exhibitions — currently photography from the 1930s.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: One change from your leaflet: the working loom demonstration is no longer at three. It now runs twice, at half eleven and at two, and lasts about twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: Photography is welcome throughout, but switch your flash off on the second floor — the prints up there are light-sensitive.

transcript.speaker: Guide
transcript.text: The lift reaches the first floor only. For step-free access to the second, speak to any staff member in a green lanyard and they'll take you up in the service lift.

questions.prompt: 89. When does the loom demonstration now run?

options.text: At half eleven and at two

questions.explanationVi: 'It now runs twice, at half eleven and at two'. Ba giờ là giờ CŨ in trên tờ rơi.

options.text: It is allowed, but without flash on the second floor.
It is banned throughout the museum.
It is allowed on the ground floor only.

questions.explanationVi: 'Photography is welcome throughout, but switch your flash off on the second floor'.

questions.prompt: 91. How can a visitor reach the second floor without stairs?

options.text: The main lift goes to all floors.
By asking a staff member in a green lanyard

questions.explanationVi: 'The lift reaches the first floor only… speak to any staff member in a green lanyard'.

title: Part 4 — Talk 8: service advertisement
instructionsVi: Quảng cáo có nhiều điều kiện loại trừ ở cuối, nói rất nhanh.
promptEn: Listen to the advertisement and answer questions 92 through 94.

transcript.speaker: Voice
transcript.text: Is your accounts team still chasing paper invoices? Kestrel Ledger can take that off your desk.

transcript.speaker: Voice
transcript.text: We handle invoice capture, approval routing and payment scheduling, and we integrate with the four systems most mid-sized firms already use.

transcript.speaker: Voice
transcript.text: Set-up is normally twelve hundred pounds. This quarter, we're waiving it for firms processing more than five hundred invoices a month.

transcript.speaker: Voice
transcript.text: That waiver covers set-up only. Data migration from your old system is quoted separately, and the monthly licence is unchanged.

transcript.speaker: Voice
transcript.text: Book a demonstration at kestrelledger dot example. Demonstrations run Tuesdays and Thursdays, and take about forty minutes.

questions.prompt: 92. Who qualifies for the waived set-up fee?

options.text: Firms processing more than 500 invoices a month
Firms using one of the four supported systems

questions.explanationVi: 'we're waiving it for firms processing more than five hundred invoices a month'.

questions.prompt: 93. What does the waiver NOT cover?

options.text: Data migration and the monthly licence

questions.explanationVi: 'Data migration from your old system is quoted separately, and the monthly licence is unchanged'.

title: Part 4 — Talk 9: with a sales table on the test paper
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 4 · Talk 9, kèm bảng trên đề (câu 95–97)
instructionsVi: Dạng 'Look at the graphic' khó: người nói KHÔNG đọc con số nào, chỉ mô tả bằng thứ hạng và quan hệ.
promptEn:
Listen to the presentation and answer questions 95 through 97. Refer to the table below where indicated.

REGIONAL SALES, Q3 (£m)
North — 12.4
South — 8.9
East — 15.1
West — 9.7

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Thanks. Headlines only; we'll go into detail in the breakouts.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: The quarter came in slightly ahead of plan overall, but the regional picture is uneven and that's what needs a decision today.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Our strongest region is performing well and I'm not going to spend time on it, because nothing there requires anything from this group.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: The one I want to discuss is the region that came in lowest. That result is not a surprise — we closed two depots there in June — but the recovery has been slower than the model predicted. We now think the second half of next year is realistic, rather than the first.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: One caveat before questions. The figures in front of you exclude the Meridian acquisition, which completed in August. Including it would add roughly two million to the eastern total, so please don't quote these externally without that note.

questions.prompt: 95. Look at the graphic. Which region does the speaker want to discuss?
questions.explanationVi: Vùng có kết quả THẤP NHẤT là South (8,9). Con số không được đọc ra, phải tự tra bảng.

questions.prompt: 96. Why does the speaker skip the strongest region?

options.text: No decision is required from this group about it.

questions.explanationVi: 'nothing there requires anything from this group'.

options.text: The figures exclude an acquisition worth about £2m in the East.
The figures include an August acquisition.
The figures are provisional and will be restated.

questions.explanationVi: 'The figures… exclude the Meridian acquisition… would add roughly two million to the eastern total'. Chú ý 'exclude', dễ nghe nhầm thành 'include'.

title: Part 4 — Talk 10: closing remarks at a review meeting
instructionsVi: Bài cuối của Listening. Người nói phân biệt hai khái niệm dễ bị gộp và rút ra một kết luận có điều kiện.
promptEn: Listen to the closing remarks and answer questions 98 through 100.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Before we finish, one observation about how we've been reading the complaint data.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: Complaints are up eighteen per cent. Everyone in this room has treated that as bad news, and I want to separate two things that have been getting merged.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: One is whether more things are going wrong. The other is whether more people are telling us. We introduced the in-app reporting button in February, and the rise starts in February.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: So it is quite possible that the underlying failure rate hasn't moved at all and we're simply hearing about more of it — which, if true, is good news wearing a bad disguise.

transcript.speaker: Speaker
transcript.text: The action I want is to compare complaint volume against warranty claims, which are recorded independently of the button. If warranty claims are flat, we have our answer.

questions.prompt: 98. What two things does the speaker separate?

options.text: More failures occurring, and more failures being reported

questions.explanationVi: 'One is whether more things are going wrong. The other is whether more people are telling us'.

questions.prompt: 99. What does the speaker mean by 'good news wearing a bad disguise'?

options.text: The complaint data has been falsified.
Complaints will fall again next quarter.
The reporting button should be removed.
A rise in complaints may reflect better reporting, not worse quality.

questions.explanationVi: Nếu tỉ lệ hỏng không đổi mà chỉ có nhiều người phản ánh hơn, thì con số tăng thực ra là dấu hiệu tốt.

questions.prompt: 100. What action does the speaker request?
questions.explanationVi: 'compare complaint volume against warranty claims, which are recorded independently of the button'.
